meta.note: How each state's Medicaid program funds Graduate Medical Education (GME). Shown in the hospital picker when a hospital has no per-hospital Medicaid GME figure, so a program director still gets the state's funding picture, what public data exists, and where to find it. Facts are sourced (primarily the AAMC 2022 50-State Survey plus state Medicaid agencies); a null field means it was not confidently found. Not legal or official guidance. Includes the 50 states, DC, and Puerto Rico.
meta.primarySources: AAMC Medicaid GME 50-State Survey (2022); MACPAC; state Medicaid agencies

AK.summary: Per the AAMC 2022 survey, Alaska made no Medicaid GME payments in 2022; it has no risk-based managed care and made no FFS GME payments. Alaska relies on the multi-state WWAMI program for physician training. No public per-hospital Medicaid GME data exists because no such payments are made.

AL.summary: The AAMC 2022 50-State Survey confirms Alabama made no Medicaid GME payments in 2022 under either fee-for-service or managed care; Alabama is listed among seven states that did not pay for GME, and its Medicaid program has no comprehensive risk-based managed care. No public per-hospital GME payment data exists because no GME payments are made.
AL.sourceName: AAMC, Medicaid Graduate Medical Education Payments: Results From the 2022 50-State Survey (Tables 1 and 15)

AR.mechanism: FFS supplemental payments (no risk-based managed care)
AR.summary: Arkansas funds Medicaid GME entirely through fee-for-service and operates no comprehensive risk-based managed care, so there are no managed-care GME payments. Payments recognize direct (DGME) but not indirect (IME), delivered as part of the hospital base rate and as a UPL supplemental payment from the State-Operated Teaching Hospital's DGME costs times its Medicaid-patient-day ratio (concentrated in UAMS). The only public figure is a state total of $10.5M for SFY2022 from the AAMC survey; no public per-hospital file exists.

AZ.mechanism: Both FFS and managed care (IGT/IGA-funded, with state General Fund share)
AZ.summary: AHCCCS (Arizona Medicaid) funds both Direct (DME) and Indirect (IME) medical education and publishes actual per-hospital payments by academic year. The non-federal share is supplied largely through Intergovernmental Transfers/Agreements (IGT/IGA) from counties, districts, and universities, plus a state General Fund share, matched with federal Medicaid dollars. Per-hospital direct and indirect amounts are included directly in this tool.

CA.summary: Medi-Cal makes GME payments to designated public hospitals (DPHs) in recognition of the Medi-Cal managed care share of both direct (DGME) and indirect (IME) GME costs, effective January 1, 2017, with the nonfederal share funded by voluntary intergovernmental transfers (IGTs). Per the AAMC 2022 survey, California made $415.1M in total Medicaid GME payments in 2022, all as explicit managed care payments and $0 under fee-for-service. No public per-hospital GME payment dollar file is published; only statewide totals and per-FTE methodology are available.

CO.summary: Colorado Medicaid (HCPF) makes GME payments recognizing direct (DGME) costs only, paid directly to hospitals with GME programs rather than through MCOs/RAEs. The AAMC 2022 survey reports $11.6M under FFS and $2.1M explicit managed care, totaling $13.7M. HCPF publishes hospital-level supplemental-payment schedules (CHASE program), but a GME-specific per-hospital dollar list was not confirmed, so per-hospital GME data is treated as unavailable.

CT.summary: Connecticut Medicaid recognizes both DGME and IME costs and pays GME entirely under fee-for-service, since Connecticut runs Medicaid under a self-insured/ASO model with no comprehensive risk-based managed care. Per the AAMC 2022 survey, total GME payments were about $164.5 million, all FFS, distributed as supplemental payments to teaching hospitals within the federal upper payment limit, financed by state general fund. No public per-hospital GME dollar file was located.

DC.summary: The District of Columbia Medicaid program recognizes both direct and indirect costs and pays under both fee-for-service and managed care. IME is folded into the hospital base rate and DGME is paid per Medicaid discharge under FFS, while under managed care DC makes explicit GME payments directly to teaching hospitals. The AAMC 2022 survey (reporting DC's SFY 2021 figures) shows $24.4M FFS plus $50.9M explicit managed care, totaling $75.4M; no public per-hospital breakdown was located.

DE.summary: Delaware Medicaid recognizes GME costs but does not distinguish direct from indirect. It pays teaching hospitals as part of the hospital base rate under FFS and recognizes GME implicitly within MCO capitation rates under managed care. The AAMC 2022 survey reports $3.2M FFS plus $11.8M implicit in managed care, totaling $15.0M; no public per-hospital GME file was located.

FL.summary: Florida Medicaid funds GME through several appropriated programs administered by the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA), chiefly the Statewide Medicaid Residency Program (SMRP), the GME Startup Bonus Program, the Slots for Doctors Program, and a Medicaid Indirect Medical Education (IME) Program created in 2022 that mirrors Medicare IME. AHCA publishes annual SMRP reconciliation calculations that list each participating hospital by name and Medicaid ID with its specific dollar allocation; the SFY2023-24 SMRP distribution totaled about $190.3M. Per OPPAGA (Dec 2023), combined state GME-program appropriations reached about $431M in SFY2023-24, and including the state IME Program brought the combined total to roughly $1,044M. Florida recognizes both direct FTE-based resident-training costs (SMRP) and indirect case-mix costs (IME Program).
FL.sourceName: OPPAGA, Graduate Medical Education in Florida (Report No. 23-GME, December 2023); AHCA SMRP reconciliation

GA.summary: Georgia Medicaid pays GME under fee-for-service, recognizing both direct (DGME) and indirect (IME) costs, distributed to teaching hospitals as UPL-based supplemental payments; under managed care it recognizes IME. The AAMC 2022 survey reported $55.0M in FFS GME payments, with managed-care GME unreported, so the total understates actual spending. No public per-hospital GME dollar file was located on the Georgia DCH site.

HI.mechanism: Managed care (QUEST Integration); GME treatment not independently confirmed
HI.summary: Hawaii is counted among the states making Medicaid GME payments in 2022 (not on the non-payer list). Its Medicaid program (Med-QUEST) is delivered almost entirely through QUEST Integration managed care, and inpatient acute services shifted to APR-DRG payment under SPA 21-0011 (effective July 2022). No public per-hospital GME dollar file or state-level total was located, and the direct/indirect breakdown could not be confirmed.

IA.summary: Iowa Medicaid funds GME through both fee-for-service and managed care, recognizing direct and indirect costs; the FFS Graduate Medical Education and Disproportionate Share Fund pays qualifying teaching hospitals outside of claims, and payments also flow through IA Health Link managed care. The AAMC 2022 survey reports Iowa's total Medicaid GME at $75.6M (SFY2021). A newer managed-care GME supplemental program (SPA IA-25-0014, effective July 1, 2025) is projected around $271M combined computable annually, but that is forward-looking, not audited. Only methodology is published; no public per-hospital dollar schedule was located.

ID.mechanism: Medicaid GME funding program (state appropriation leveraged with federal match)
ID.summary: Idaho is a Medicaid GME-paying state (not on the AAMC non-payer list). Under its GME strategic plan, Idaho contributes roughly one-third of estimated resident training cost via a per-resident amount (about $60,000 of an estimated $180,000/resident) and uses a Medicaid mechanism that leverages state funds with a roughly 70/30 federal match. No public per-hospital GME dollar schedule or state-level total was located; direct-vs-indirect treatment could not be confirmed.
ID.sourceName: AAMC 2022 50-State Survey; Idaho State Board of Education GME 10-Year Strategic Plan

IL.mechanism: FFS (DGME + IME in DRG rates); managed care embedded in capitation
IL.summary: Illinois Medicaid makes GME payments and recognizes both direct (DGME) and indirect (IME) costs, with medical-education factors built into its hospital DRG rate methodology under 89 Ill. Adm. Code 148. In the AAMC 2022 survey, Illinois reported $158.5M in total Medicaid GME payments, all on a fee-for-service basis; managed care GME paid through MCO capitation was not readily available and is not included. The AAMC report provides only a statewide total, not a public per-hospital GME dollar breakdown.

IN.summary: Indiana Medicaid makes GME payments recognizing direct (DGME) costs only, under both fee-for-service and managed care. Per the AAMC 2022 survey, Indiana paid $15.0M under FFS and $24.0M in explicit managed-care payments, totaling $39.0M. No public per-hospital GME dollar list was located; Indiana's other hospital supplemental programs (Hospital Assessment Fee, State Directed Payments) are distinct from GME.

KS.mechanism: Both FFS and managed care (mostly embedded in capitation)
KS.summary: Kansas funds Medicaid GME almost entirely through its KanCare managed care program, with GME dollars embedded implicitly in MCO capitation rather than paid as discrete supplemental payments; a small FFS component (about $0.30M) covers payments to teaching physicians. The AAMC 2022 survey reports Kansas recognizes both direct and indirect costs and estimates total 2022 Medicaid GME at $23.8M, of which $23.5M is implicit in capitation and only $0.30M explicit. Because the managed-care GME is buried in capitation without identifiable per-hospital rates, no public per-hospital file exists.

KY.summary: Kentucky Medicaid recognizes both DGME and IME costs and pays GME under both fee-for-service and managed care, with managed-care GME paid directly to teaching hospitals. Per the AAMC 2022 survey (Kentucky data for SFY 2021), total GME payments were about $116.3 million, overwhelmingly through managed care ($105.6M direct-to-hospital) versus $10.7M FFS. Nonfederal share is financed by state general fund plus local government contributions. No public per-hospital GME dollar file was located.

LA.summary: Louisiana Medicaid recognizes only direct (DGME) costs and pays GME exclusively under fee-for-service; it does not leave GME in the MCO capitation base. Per the AAMC 2022 survey, total FFS GME payments were about $23.9 million, distributed to major and minor teaching hospitals partly as base rate and partly as a separate payment. State Plan Amendment attachments describe methodology but do not publish a clean per-hospital GME dollar schedule.
LA.sourceName: AAMC 2022 50-State Survey (Tables 1, 6, 11); Louisiana Department of Health State Plan

MA.summary: Massachusetts made no Medicaid GME payments in 2022 under either fee-for-service or managed care, per the AAMC 2022 survey, and is one of only seven states (with AL, AK, NH, ND, RI, WY) that do not fund Medicaid GME. This is notable because Massachusetts ranks among the top 10 states for both teaching hospitals and physician residents. With no payments, there is no per-hospital GME data.

MD.mechanism: Embedded in HSCRC all-payer hospital rates
MD.summary: Maryland Medicaid pays for GME but does not distinguish direct from indirect costs; GME cost is built into the state's HSCRC all-payer hospital rates, so each Medicaid capitation cell embeds the historic average GME cost for enrollees. The AAMC 2022 survey reports $59.8M with no FFS/managed-care breakdown. Because Medicaid GME is embedded in rates rather than paid as a separate line, no public per-hospital Medicaid-GME dollar list exists; roughly 58% historically went to Johns Hopkins and the University of Maryland Medical System.

ME.summary: Under MaineCare Benefits Manual Section 45 (DRG methodology effective July 1, 2024), each teaching hospital receives a custom GME add-on rate inclusive of both direct and indirect medical education costs, derived from FY2022 as-filed Medicare Cost Report data at 100% of MaineCare's share of GME costs, applied per discharge. Maine DHHS publishes the per-hospital GME add-on amounts (per-discharge add-ons, not annual totals): e.g., Maine Medical Center $1,082, MaineGeneral $916, Central Maine $355, Northern Light Eastern Maine $205.
ME.sourceName: Maine DHHS / MaineCare, Section 45 Hospital Services GME Add-On

MI.summary: Michigan Medicaid funds GME through both a fee-for-service GME pool and managed care (implicit in MCO capitation rates), and is one of only three states that also make GME payments to medical schools (via the MIDocs consortia). It does not distinguish DGME from IME. The AAMC 2022 survey reported $162.9M total ($31.2M FFS plus $131.7M implicit managed care). MDHHS posts annual per-hospital GME Distribution spreadsheets on its Medicaid Inpatient Hospital Providers page.

MN.mechanism: Both FFS and managed care (MERC program)
MN.summary: Minnesota funds GME through its Medical Education and Research Costs (MERC) program, which does not distinguish direct from indirect costs and distributes funds using a Medicaid-revenue-share formula (Minn. Stat. 62J.692). The AAMC 2022 survey reports $78.5M ($7.5M FFS plus $71.0M explicit managed care); after CMS declined to renew the 1115 waiver, the 2023 Legislature moved most funding into a Medical Education component of Medicaid FFS hospital rates. The public MERC 2025 Distribution Report shows total funding of $59.2M and lists per-facility award amounts by name (e.g., Hennepin County Medical Center $7.83M; Mayo Clinic $5.67M).
MN.sourceName: AAMC 2022 50-State Survey (aggregate); Minnesota Dept. of Health MERC Distribution Annual Report 2025 (per-hospital)

MO.summary: MO HealthNet (Missouri Medicaid) makes GME payments recognizing direct (DGME) costs only, entirely through fee-for-service; it reported no managed-care GME. The AAMC 2022 survey reports $179.4M, one of the largest state Medicaid GME programs. The methodology is set in regulation (13 CSR 70-15.010) with an institution-and-resident-based amount calculated per hospital each state fiscal year, but no public per-hospital dollar list was located. (A separate Missouri DHSS GME workforce program exists outside Medicaid.)

MS.summary: Mississippi Medicaid funds GME through fee-for-service direct GME supplemental payments to in-state accredited teaching hospitals, paid at a flat $65,000 per resident FTE, distributed quarterly (SPA 23-0017). Through 2024 the state did not reimburse indirect (IME) and made no managed-care GME payments; SPA 25-0007 (effective April 1, 2025) newly added an IME payment. The most recent published state total is $39.9M (all DGME/FFS) from the AAMC 2022 survey. No public per-hospital distribution file was found, only the per-FTE rate.
MS.sourceName: AAMC 2022 50-State Survey; Mississippi Division of Medicaid SPAs 23-0017 and 25-0007

MT.summary: Montana Medicaid makes GME payments only under fee-for-service (no risk-based managed care), as supplemental payments to teaching hospitals up to the upper payment limit using a per-resident method; it does not distinguish direct from indirect costs. The AAMC 2022 survey reports total Medicaid GME payments of $6.4 million (combined federal and state funds); no public per-hospital breakdown was located.

NC.summary: North Carolina Medicaid pays GME only under fee-for-service (no managed-care GME payments), recognizing both DGME and IME costs for teaching hospitals. The AAMC 2022 survey reported $308.2M in total Medicaid GME payments, all FFS. NC settles GME through hospital cost reports; no public per-hospital GME dollar-amount file was located.

ND.summary: Per the AAMC 2022 survey, North Dakota made no Medicaid GME payments under either fee-for-service or managed care in 2022; it is one of only seven non-paying states. No public per-hospital Medicaid GME data exists because no such payments are made.

NE.summary: Nebraska Medicaid makes a fee-for-service GME supplemental payment to eligible teaching hospitals (those reporting resident training on their most recent Medicare Cost Report). The state plan calculates direct GME payments from the hospital's direct GME cost times its Medicaid patient load, with designated UNMC-affiliated teaching hospitals receiving 1.15 times the computed amount. The methodology is public in the state plan (SPA NE 22-0002), but no public list of per-hospital GME dollar amounts was found.
NE.sourceName: Nebraska Medicaid State Plan, Attachment 4.19-A / SPA NE 22-0002

NH.summary: New Hampshire made no Medicaid GME payments in 2022 per the AAMC survey, which lists NH among the seven non-paying states. The program does not recognize direct or indirect GME costs and makes no FFS or directed managed-care GME payments. No per-hospital GME data exists because no such payments are made.

NJ.summary: New Jersey Medicaid makes no FFS GME payments; GME is funded under managed care as explicit directed payments to teaching hospitals, administered through the state DOH Health Care Subsidy Fund as GME/GME-S/GME-T subsidies, recognizing both DGME and IME. The AAMC 2022 survey reported $242.0M (SFY2023). NJ DOH publishes per-hospital GME subsidy allocation files; the SFY2025 file totals about $218M across roughly 45 named hospitals.
NJ.sourceName: AAMC 2022 50-State Survey (Table 11); NJ DOH Hospital Subsidies

NM.summary: New Mexico Medicaid makes GME payments to qualifying teaching hospitals entirely through fee-for-service, recognizing both direct and indirect costs. Per the AAMC 2022 survey, New Mexico paid $188.7M in total Medicaid GME in SFY2022 (100% FFS, $0 managed care), 11th nationally. Its state plan sets a per-hospital IME/DGME formula (quarterly IME payments to hospitals with at least 5% Medicaid inpatient utilization), but the state publishes only methodology, not a per-hospital dollar distribution. New Mexico awaits federal approval of a Centennial Care 1115 waiver amendment to fund GME expansion under managed care.

NV.summary: Nevada Medicaid funds Direct GME through a fee-for-service supplemental payment program administered by DHCFP, with a parallel managed-care GME methodology (SPA NV-17-010, approved 2017) financed via intergovernmental transfers plus federal match. In SFY2024, $31,549,215 in GME supplemental payments was distributed statewide (down 5.42% from $33.36M in SFY2023). Nevada recognized direct GME only through SFY2024 and added a separate IME supplemental program beginning SFY2025. Public per-hospital amounts appear annually in DHCFP's statutory Report on the Activities and Operations of Nevada Hospitals (Exhibit 1A), which breaks out a GME column by hospital.
NV.sourceName: Nevada DHCFP Report on the Activities and Operations of Nevada Hospitals (NRS 449.520), SFY2024

NY.summary: New York operates the nation's largest Medicaid GME program. Per the AAMC 2022 survey, New York's Medicaid GME payments totaled about $1.92 billion in 2022, the highest of any state and roughly one-fourth of the national total. New York recognizes and pays for both direct (DGME) and indirect (IME) costs under both fee-for-service and managed care, with supplemental reimbursements to teaching hospitals administered through the state's Public Goods Pool/Professional Education Pool framework. New York DOH publishes intern/resident FTE counts by hospital, but no consolidated public file lists actual GME dollar payments per hospital.

OH.summary: Ohio Medicaid pays for GME through a medical education add-on built into its fee-for-service inpatient hospital (APR-DRG) rate methodology under Ohio Administrative Code Rule 5160-2-67. The methodology explicitly recognizes both direct (DGME) and indirect (IME) costs, computing a per-discharge, case-mix-adjusted add-on for each qualifying hospital. To qualify, a hospital must operate an approved medical education program whose costs were reflected in its SFY2014 Ohio Medicaid cost report. No public per-hospital GME payment dollar file and no confidently-sourced recent statewide Medicaid GME total were located.
OH.sourceName: Ohio Administrative Code Rule 5160-2-67, Ohio Department of Medicaid

OK.summary: Oklahoma Medicaid (SoonerCare) recognizes both DGME and IME costs and pays GME entirely under fee-for-service as supplemental payments, since Oklahoma operates no comprehensive risk-based managed care. Per the AAMC 2022 survey, total FFS GME payments were about $46.6 million. OHCA makes a Direct Medical Education payment to teaching hospitals with approved residency programs and an Indirect Medical Education adjustment to major teaching hospitals (150+ FTE residents). The OHCA page describes methodology but publishes no per-hospital dollar amounts.
OK.sourceName: AAMC 2022 50-State Survey (Tables 1, 11); Oklahoma Health Care Authority

OR.summary: Oregon Medicaid recognizes both DGME and IME costs and pays GME under both fee-for-service and managed care, with managed-care GME paid directly to teaching hospitals. Per the AAMC 2022 survey, total GME payments were about $151.0 million, most ($135.5M) as explicit direct managed-care payments plus $15.5M FFS. FFS GME for public teaching hospitals is governed by OAR 410-125-0142. No public per-hospital GME dollar schedule was located.
OR.sourceName: AAMC 2022 50-State Survey (Tables 1, 7, 11); Oregon Administrative Rules OAR 410-125-0142

PA.summary: Pennsylvania Medicaid makes GME payments. It reimburses teaching hospitals for direct medical education (DME) costs on a fee-for-service, cost-based basis under Medicare cost principles (55 Pa. Code Chapter 1163), and beginning FY2024-2025 established separate Inpatient and Outpatient Indirect Medical Education (IME) supplemental payment programs totaling $261.9M in combined state and federal funds (inpatient $184.7M + outpatient $77.2M), limited to acute-care teaching hospitals in Philadelphia. Pennsylvania also makes academic medical center directed payments through its managed care contracts. Published notices set program-level allocations and formulas rather than per-hospital GME dollar amounts, and no single combined DME+IME statewide GME total is published.
PA.sourceName: Pennsylvania Bulletin (Vol. 54, No. 27), PA Department of Human Services

PR.mechanism: US territory — Medicaid funded under a capped federal block grant (not the 50-state FMAP structure)
PR.summary: Puerto Rico is a US territory whose Medicaid program is financed under a capped federal block grant rather than the open-ended federal match used by the 50 states, and it was not included in the AAMC 2022 50-State Survey. Whether and how Puerto Rico Medicaid funds graduate medical education, and any per-hospital amounts, were not established from public sources here; treat the Medicare GME figures above as the confirmed data and consult ASES / the Puerto Rico Department of Health for Medicaid GME specifics.
PR.sourceName: AAMC, Graduate Medical Education (GME): Payments to Teaching Hospitals (overview)

RI.summary: Rhode Island made no Medicaid GME payments in 2022 per the AAMC survey, which lists RI among the seven non-paying states. The program does not recognize direct or indirect GME costs and makes no FFS or directed managed-care GME payments. No per-hospital GME data exists because no such payments are made.

SC.summary: South Carolina Medicaid recognizes both DGME and IME costs and pays GME under both fee-for-service and managed care. Per the AAMC 2022 survey, total GME payments were about $296.6 million ($90.2M FFS, $68.9M explicit managed-care payments to teaching hospitals, and $132.5M implicit in MCO capitation). SC is notable in that MCO capitation GME was distributed to teaching physicians rather than hospitals. Effective October 1, 2025, SCDHHS moved to a standardized statewide per-resident amount (about $80,000/FTE) plus incentives. Public documents describe methodology, not a per-hospital dollar list.
SC.sourceName: AAMC 2022 50-State Survey (Tables 1, 11); SCDHHS GME program materials

SD.summary: South Dakota Medicaid makes GME payments only under fee-for-service (no managed care), using a modified Medicare hospital method and not distinguishing direct from indirect costs. Payments go to teaching hospitals as supplemental payments up to the upper payment limit, plus a separate payment to a USD Sanford School of Medicine rural family medicine residency. The AAMC 2022 survey reports $3.1 million total; no public per-hospital breakdown was located.

TN.summary: TennCare (Tennessee Medicaid) is fully managed care, so it makes no fee-for-service GME payments; it distributes GME through the managed care system and does not distinguish direct from indirect costs. Payments come from a fixed pool of $48,000,000 annually, split into two $24M sub-pools (one weighted by each hospital's share of TennCare adjusted days, one by filled resident positions at eligible Tennessee teaching hospitals). The AAMC survey reports $48.0M for SFY2023. The state plan amendment publishes methodology but no public per-hospital dollar list was located.

TX.summary: Texas Medicaid pays for GME and recognizes both direct (DGME) and indirect (IME) costs under fee-for-service and managed care. Urban teaching hospitals receive an IME add-on to Medicaid inpatient reimbursement, while public teaching hospitals receive supplemental DGME payments financed via intergovernmental transfers and state General Revenue; in 2023 HHSC added a GME supplemental payment program for non-government teaching hospitals. The AAMC 2022 survey reports Texas total Medicaid GME of $226.6M. HHSC publishes supplemental-payment reports (Rider 14(B)) and GME rate packets, but a public file listing GME dollars by individual hospital could not be independently verified (HHSC servers block automated retrieval).

UT.summary: Utah Medicaid funds GME primarily through quarterly fee-for-service Direct GME supplemental payments to nine teaching hospitals under State Plan Attachment 4.19-A, using state general funds matched with federal dollars. Utah publishes downloadable per-hospital GME Calculation Excel workbooks (SFY2022-2024) showing each hospital's exact allocation, totaling about $6.54M for SFY2024, with University of Utah Hospital receiving roughly 74%. Historically Utah recognized only direct (DGME) costs under FFS; effective July 1, 2024 a new managed-care directed payment to University of Utah Hospitals and Clinics (SPA UT-24-0013) added recognition of both direct and indirect costs.
UT.sourceName: Utah DHHS Medicaid Inpatient Hospital GME program (per-hospital); AAMC 2022 50-State Survey

VA.summary: Virginia Medicaid funds GME under both fee-for-service and managed care (explicit payments to teaching hospitals), recognizing both DGME and IME; it also makes competitive supplemental payments for high-needs-specialty residency slots (up to $100,000 per resident per year). The AAMC 2022 survey reported $449.9M total ($180.3M FFS plus $269.7M explicit managed care), the third-highest GME-spending state. DMAS publishes a GME Hospital Residency Summary Report listing residents by hospital (counts, not payment dollars).

VT.summary: Vermont Medicaid makes GME payments under fee-for-service and recognizes both direct and indirect costs; it makes no separate managed-care GME payments. Payments are supplemental payments to teaching hospitals up to the upper payment limit, benefiting principally the University of Vermont Medical Center. The AAMC 2022 survey reports $30.0 million total; no public per-hospital GME file was located.

WA.summary: Washington Medicaid pays GME to hospitals using a DRG cost-based method embedded in each hospital's base rate rather than as a separate GME pool, recognizing both DGME and IME. Because GME is bundled into the hospital base rate and varies per claim, the state told the AAMC it was impractical to tabulate GME amounts; Washington reported no state total (Unreported in 2022) and there is no public per-hospital GME dollar figure.

WI.summary: Wisconsin Medicaid makes GME payments recognizing direct (DGME) costs only. The AAMC 2022 survey reports $33.0M in explicit FFS GME payments plus $36.2M recognized implicitly within managed-care capitation, totaling $69.2M. No public per-hospital Medicaid-GME dollar list was located; note that Wisconsin's DHS 'Grow Our Own' GME grant program is a distinct state workforce initiative, not the Medicaid GME payments counted here.

WV.mechanism: Makes Medicaid GME payments (methodology not independently verified)
WV.summary: West Virginia is counted among the 44 states (including DC) that made Medicaid GME payments in 2022 per the AAMC survey; it is not on the non-paying list. Hospital reimbursement is governed by BMS Provider Manual Chapter 600, but a public itemized GME methodology and per-hospital schedule could not be independently confirmed. No public per-hospital GME dollar file or state-level total was located.

WY.summary: Per the AAMC 2022 survey, Wyoming made no Medicaid GME payments in 2022; it has no risk-based managed care and made no FFS GME payments. Wyoming relies on the multi-state WWAMI program and a UW-affiliated family medicine residency. No public per-hospital Medicaid GME data exists because no such payments are made.
